correctness.rationale: For unit mixed-subset simplex sums, coordinate ordering expresses u as positive nested centered cuts; linearity of widths plus strict Euclidean triangle inequality forces every optimal direction to have exactly two levels. Mixed-subset counting gives W(s,t)=B−(2^s−1)(2^t−1)−(2^{p−s}−1)(2^{q−t}−1); norms give exact finite ratio. Analytic inequalities exclude noncentral cuts for n≥128, midpoint convexity gives central equality cases, and exhaustive exact integer finite search covers all 4≤n≤127. Independently reimplemented and ran the complete finite search from scratch: exactly 3906 p,q profiles and 5,870,718 cut profiles, all claimed minimizers, no floating tolerances. Formula and large-q asymptotics follow from tube counts.
residual_risks: Large-n proof relies on the published bound chain (8)-(10) rather than finite enumeration; independent calculation is exhaustive only through n=127. Alternative affine realizations or weights can change the width.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Previously published same-model genuine-biclique inradius concerns distance to facets, not minimum distance between parallel supporting hyperplanes; it does not imply width. Previously published 15-total-vertex stellohedron crossover has p=1, explicitly outside p,q≥2, and 1-variable leaf cut counts fail for genuine bicliques with two color classes.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge genuine biclique p,q≥2 width phase and full minimizing-normal classification are not covered by Postnikov generalized permutohedron construction, star p=1 prior width theorem, biclique inball theorem, or biclique graph diameter calculations. The coincidence of n=15 with star crossover does not imply the two-color result: W(s,t) has additional mixed terms.
